themes_detail.label: Tree hazards spike sharply
themes_detail.summary: Damaged and overgrown tree complaints spiked dramatically THIS WEEK in Parkchester/Soundview, with 8 damaged tree reports (vs. 2.4 weekly average) and 5 overgrown tree reports (vs. 1.9 weekly average)—a combined 237% and 167% increase—suggesting recent storm damage or neglected maintenance creating public safety risks.
evidence: Damaged Tree complaints: 8 THIS WEEK vs. 2.4 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 3.13, +237%)
Overgrown Tree/Branches complaints: 5 THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 2.97, +167%)
13 tree-related complaints in single week suggests acute trigger (weather event, deferred maintenance, or both)
reporting_angles: Did recent weather (storms, wind) cause the spike? Interview NYC Parks Department about emergency response and timeline for inspections.
Map tree complaints geographically—are they concentrated in certain blocks or near schools/parks? Interview residents about visibility of hazards.

themes_detail.label: Mobile food vendors suddenly proliferating
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints exploded THIS WEEK to 4 reports (vs. 0.6 weekly average)—a 540% spike—signaling either aggressive new vendor activity or a new enforcement crackdown, with significant implications for street commerce and community livability.
evidence: Mobile Food Vendor complaints: 4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 4.85, +540%)
Concurrent spike in Vendor Enforcement complaints: 10 last week vs. 4.1 weekly average (+142%, z-score: 2.67)
Double signal suggests either unlicensed vendors entering the district or city enforcement action ramping up
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed or non-permitted food vendors setting up new locations? Interview vendors and local business owners about why the sudden increase.
Is DOHMH or the Health Department running a targeted enforcement sweep? Verify with city agencies and check permit databases.

themes_detail.label: Building and maintenance complaints surge
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use and Maintenance or Facility complaints both spiked THIS WEEK (10 and 8 reports respectively, vs. 4.2 and 2.6 weekly averages)—representing 135% and 205% increases—suggesting accelerating deterioration in rental buildings or delayed superintendent/landlord response.
evidence: Building/Use complaints: 10 THIS WEEK vs. 4.2 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 2.81, +135%)
Maintenance or Facility complaints: 8 THIS WEEK vs. 2.6 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 2.78, +205%)
18 combined complaints in one week; sustained trend would indicate systemic landlord neglect or enforcement gap
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings are generating complaints most frequently via HPD and DOHMH records; are they owned by the same landlords or management companies?
Interview residents in affected buildings about what specifically is broken (heat systems, elevator maintenance, structural issues?) and how long issues have persisted.

themes_detail.label: Curb and street infrastructure degrading
themes_detail.summary: Curb Condition complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average—a 300% spike—indicating rapid deterioration of streetscape infrastructure that could signal deferred DOT maintenance or impact pedestrian/vehicular safety.
evidence: Curb Condition complaints: 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 3.4, +300%)
Street Condition remains a top 311 complaint category overall (869 over 90 days), suggesting chronic infrastructure issues
Spike this week may reflect recent inspection or new damage pattern
reporting_angles: Walk affected blocks to photograph curb damage; cross-reference with DOT maintenance schedules and budget allocations.
Interview DOT about condition of district's curbs and timeline for repairs; check if pothole/curb damage complaints have been chronically underfunded.

themes_detail.label: Heat complaints plummet seasonally
themes_detail.summary: Heat/Hot Water complaints dropped 88% THIS WEEK to 24 reports (vs. 191.2 weekly average)—a sharp seasonal decline typical of warming weather—but this remains the #3 complaint category overall (2,128 over 90 days), indicating underlying housing code violations that will resurface when temperatures fall.
evidence: Heat/Hot Water complaints: 24 THIS WEEK vs. 191.2 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: -3.32, -88% decline)
Heat/Hot Water is #3 complaint category by volume over 90 days (2,128 total complaints), indicating endemic issue
Seasonal pattern: spike in winter, drop in spring/summer masks failure to address root causes (landlord non-compliance, aging infrastructure)
reporting_angles: Identify buildings with repeat heat violations over multiple winters via HPD database; are any landlords chronic violators? Are violations leading to fines or building takeovers?
Interview tenants about cold apartments during winter months and whether landlords are making repairs or residents are paying for heating; investigate if code enforcement is adequate.
